editorial:
Imagine being fifty years old but still feeling like a teenager who only cares about fast bikes and hanging out with the boys. That is exactly where you find Michel. He spends most of his time with his grown son, Leo, and a group of friends who are basically just as immature as he is. The vibe is light and funny, but it hits you with a real punch when Michel finds out he has a new baby with his ex. Now, he has to figure out how to grow up fast so he does not mess up this second chance at being a father.

You will love how the acting feels real and not forced. The chemistry between the father and son is the best part of the whole story. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the emotional payoff makes it worth your time. It is a great pick for anyone who likes stories about family mistakes and redemption.
endingExplained: By the end, Michel finally stops acting like a child and accepts his responsibilities. He realizes that being a hero is not about motorcycles or looking cool, but about showing up for his kids. He makes peace with his ex and commits to being a present father for the baby. The movie wraps up with a sweet moment showing that it is never too late to change your ways and grow up.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about messy families and second chances.
